messages:
zoe: quick sync — hitting a weird one with AbortController + auth refresh when using streaming in node. Abort signal cancels client but server keeps the stream alive (we see continued tokens in logs). anyone seen this?

mike: ugh. do you have a tiny repro? is this the fetch-based client or our native socket stream?

zoe: fetch-based wrapper. flow: token exp -> refresh token -> retry with new token. during refresh I call controller.abort() to stop the old attempt. client stops, but on server side the handler still emits tokens for ~5s.

sanjay: hmm the fetch AbortSignal should close the request stream, but if we re-open a new connection quickly maybe the server handler keeps processing the old work. are you using streaming partial responses (server-sent events / chunked) or websocket?

zoe: chunked HTTP streaming. server handler is async gen that yields tokens. I think the runtime job isn't being cancelled server-side because we never propagate the abort across our backend call to model runner.

anna: two quick thoughts: 1) make sure we forward the signal to any downstream long-running calls (eg modelRunner.run({signal})) 2) on token refresh, prefer graceful drain + cancel only if new request actually started.

mike: +1. also note node's AbortController only cancels fetch socket, doesn't magically throw inside random async code unless that code checks signal.aborted or uses APIs that accept signal.

zoe: makes sense. question — on SDK side, what's our recommended pattern for streaming + auth refresh? do we provide a helper that sequences abort -> wait for server ack -> reopen?

sanjay: we intentionally kept SDK minimal: SDK accepts an AbortSignal and will attach to underlying http request. We do not control server-side cancellation semantics. We should document "best-effort" and provide an optional handshake header X-RW-STREAM-ID so server can detect duped streams and cancel earlier ones.

anna: we also have fallback where server checks connection closed via res.writableEnded/event 'close' and cancels model workload. but there is often a few second window. For strict workloads recommend using dedicated capacity with pre-emptible tokens or an explicit cancel RPC to model host.

zoe: is it safe for SDK to call abort(), then immediately create a new request with new token? worried about orphaned server compute ramping cost.

mike: safe from correctness but you get cost leakage until server cancels. two mitigations: 1) exponential backoff for immediate retries 2) send a cancel-request header containing previous stream ID so server can nuke the in-progress job.

zoe: can someone sketch a tiny JS/Python snippet we can add to docs? something that forwards signal to downstream and includes stream-id header.

anna: sure — JS sketch:

```
const ac = new AbortController();
const streamId = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);
fetch('/v1/chat/stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`, 'X-RW-STREAM-ID': streamId },
  body: jsonBody,
  signal: ac.signal
});
// on token expiry: ac.abort(); // optional: POST /v1/stream/cancel { stream_id }
```

anna: Python sketch (requests-async / httpx):

```
import httpx
client = httpx.AsyncClient()
stream_id = 's-' + uuid.uuid4().hex
r = await client.stream('POST','/v1/chat/stream', headers={'Authorization':f'Bearer {t}','X-RW-STREAM-ID':stream_id})
# hold response.iter_text() loop, but cancel by calling client.aclose() or send a cancel RPC
```

mike: tiny note for SDK implementers: in Node, ensure you use AbortController from 'node:abort-controller' or the global to match fetch polyfill. In browsers it's built in. Also ensure retries create new controllers per attempt — don't reuse aborted controllers.

zoe: great, this is actionable. i'll add a short section to devdocs + a small helper in the JS SDK with stream-id header and optional cancel endpoint. will ping when draft is up. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy-checklist: created doc draft branch zoe/abort-auth-race. CI lint passed. remember to add e2e that simulates token-expire mid-stream.

mike: thanks — re e2e, we can fast-forward model runner clock in local infra to trigger earlier cancellation and assert no leftover jobs.

zoe: perfect, thanks all!
